title: The Lawyer Who Made Poverty a Crime—and Profited
hook: A single legal clause turned being broke into a felony, and the lawyer who wrote it owns the private prisons that cash in.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exposes a hidden system where the poor are criminalized for profit—outrage hooks, dark system reveal.

title: The Billionaire Who Bought the Patent for Happiness
hook: He owns the legal rights to a molecule that triggers joy—and charges a license fee every time you feel good.
why_this_can_go_viral: Absurd yet plausible concept sparks disbelief and shares—questions who owns your emotions.

title: The Shadow Bank That Lends Money in Secret Languages
hook: No written contracts, no spoken words—just coded whistles and hand signals. Default and you disappear without a trace.
why_this_can_go_viral: Mysterious, cinematic, and feels like a secret society—strong shareability and dark intrigue.

title: The Algorithm That Sells Your Future Pain as a Stock
hook: Hedge funds now trade 'misery futures'—betting on when you'll lose your job, get divorced, or fall ill.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploits fear of being commodified—moral outrage and 'wait, that's real?' reactions drive shares.

title: The Heir Who Had to Commit a Crime to Inherit
hook: The trust fund required a felony conviction—no crime, no cash. He chose arson. The bank filmed it.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme human behavior meets hidden wealth rules—shocking, story-driven, highly shareable.

title: The Broker Who Trades in Your Last Wishes—Without Asking
hook: He buys dying people's bucket lists and sells them to the highest bidder. You planned a trip to Paris? He owns that dream now.
why_this_can_go_viral: Eerie, personal violation—makes viewers wonder what unsaid contracts govern their own lives.

title: The Country That Taxes You Only If You're Happy
hook: Citizens who report satisfaction on surveys get a tax bill. Millions now fake depression to stay rich.
why_this_can_go_viral: Absurd twist on tax systems—darkly humorous but real enough to spark debate and shares.

title: The Fund That Only Invests When a Billionaire Dies
hook: A hedge fund tracks obituaries of the ultra-rich and buys their assets before the family knows they're gone.
why_this_can_go_viral: Morally repulsive yet fascinating system—triggers outrage and curiosity about vulture capitalism.

title: The Billionaire Who Paid Zero Tax by Becoming a Coral Reef
hook: He declared his body a marine conservation zone. The tax court agreed. Now he's technically an ecosystem.
why_this_can_go_viral: Ridiculous but true-feeling loophole—perfect for shock, shareability, and 'how is this legal?' reactions.

title: The Shadow Bank That Only Exists During Blackouts
hook: When the power grid fails, this bank activates—processing loans via handwritten ledgers in a basement. No digital trace.
why_this_can_go_viral: Apocalyptic banking mystery—feels like a dark secret society, high curiosity gap.

title: The Shell Company That Bought the Air in Your Lungs
hook: A holding company now owns the patent to a specific oxygen isotope. Every breath you take incurs a royalty—payable to a ghost.
why_this_can_go_viral: Horrifyingly plausible extension of patent trolling—viewers will share in disbelief and anger.

title: The Heir Who Had to Forget Their Family to Inherit
hook: The trust fund required total amnesia—cut all photos, burn documents, never speak their parents' names. He complied.
why_this_can_go_viral: Psychologically brutal condition—triggers deep emotional reaction and discussion about wealth's dark side.

title: The Bank That Accepts Only Secrets as Collateral
hook: No money, no property—just one dark secret. Miss a payment and they tell everyone. Default rates are 0%.
why_this_can_go_viral: Dark, personal, and universally relatable—everyone has secrets. High emotional engagement.

title: The Offshore Island Where Money Literally Grows on Trees
hook: A private island planted genetically modified trees that produce gold flakes in their sap. The harvest is tax-free.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visually stunning concept—sci-fi meets wealth. High curiosity and shareability despite lower darkness.

title: The Algorithm That Predicts Divorce—and Sells Insurance to the Spouse
hook: A secret algorithm scans your messages and spending patterns. If it predicts divorce, it offers your partner a payout—on your dime.
why_this_can_go_viral: Invades personal life—triggers paranoia and outrage. Highly relatable fear of data misuse.

title: The Lawyer Who Made It Legal to Sell Other People's Souls
hook: He drafted a contract that defines 'soul' as an intangible asset. Now investors trade soul futures on the open market.
why_this_can_go_viral: Blasphemous yet legal—sparks moral outrage and dark curiosity about what can be traded.

title: The Billionaire Who Bought a Country Just for Its Tax Code
hook: He purchased a micronation for $2 million—not for land, but for the right to write its tax laws. He made himself exempt.
why_this_can_go_viral: Real-world extreme wealth move—shows how billionaires bend sovereignty for tax avoidance.

title: The Hedge Fund That Only Trades on Your Panic Attacks
hook: A biometric algorithm buys and sells stocks the moment your heart rate spikes. Your fear is their profit signal.
why_this_can_go_viral: Invades body autonomy—creepy, personal, and totally plausible. High shock value.

title: The Trust That Pays You Only If You Never Speak Again
hook: A billionaire's son inherited $500 million on one condition: total silence for life. He hasn't said a word in 12 years.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme human cost of wealth—emotionally gripping, story-driven, highly shareable.

title: The Accountant Who Laundered Money Through a Ghost Town
hook: He bought a deserted mining town, declared every building a separate business, and funneled $800 million through 'rent' between them.
why_this_can_go_viral: Creative real-world crime—visual and intriguing. Viewers love 'how they got away with it' stories.

title: The Broker Who Sells Shares in Your Neighbor's Lottery Win
hook: He buys lottery tickets in bulk, then sells fractions to investors. If your neighbor wins, you own 0.001% of their jackpot.
why_this_can_go_viral: Relatable fantasy of winning—plus dark twist of others owning your luck. High shareability.

title: The Bank That Insures Billionaires Against Falling in Love
hook: Love is a 'liability event'—if a billionaire gets married, the policy pays out. One client collected $200 million after a divorce.
why_this_can_go_viral: Romance meets cold finance—darkly funny but real. Triggers discussion about wealth and relationships.

title: The Algorithm That Ranks Humans by 'Profitability Score'
hook: A secret credit algorithm rates you not on debt, but on how much money can be extracted from your life. A low score gets you blacklisted.
why_this_can_go_viral: Maximum dystopian fear—everyone feels the threat of being reduced to a number. High outrage and shareability.
